title: Storage & disks
blurb: Disk full, external drives, USB sticks, disk errors.

remedies.title: Disk is full or almost full
symptoms: your startup disk is almost full
remedies.why: Downloads, temporary files, old updates, photos and videos, and cloud files kept on the computer fill the disk. Under ~10% free slows everything.

steps.text: See what takes the space: the Disk map shows the biggest folders and files.
Clean temporary files, caches and old update leftovers.
Empty the Recycle Bin / Bin and clear old Downloads.
Turn on Storage Sense to clean up automatically.
System Settings › General › Storage shows recommendations (Optimise Storage, Empty Bin automatically).
Set OneDrive / iCloud Drive to keep files online only (Files On-Demand / Optimise Mac Storage).
Move large videos and old projects to an external drive.

remedies.title: External drive or USB stick doesn't show up
remedies.why: No drive letter, a format the system can't read, not enough power, or a failing drive.

steps.text: Plug straight into the computer, try another port and cable; big drives may need their own power.
Open Disk Management: if the drive is there without a letter, right-click › Change Drive Letter and Paths › Add.
Open Disk Utility: if the drive is listed but greyed, select it › Mount.
A drive formatted for a Mac (APFS) isn't readable on Windows without extra software, and Windows NTFS drives are read-only on a Mac. exFAT works on both.
Don't format a drive that has your files on it because the system asks; back it up first.
Check the drive's health.

remedies.escalate: Clicking or grinding noises: stop using the drive; a recovery service has the best chance.

remedies.title: Disk errors, "scan and fix" or a drive that's failing
remedies.why: The file system has errors (often after power loss) or the drive itself is wearing out.

steps.text: Back up important files now, before trying repairs.
Check the drive's health and errors in DeskMedic's Disks page.
Scan the drive: File Explorer › right-click the drive › Properties › Tools › Check.
Disk Utility › select the drive › First Aid.
A drive reporting health warnings should be replaced even if it still works.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT straight away if the main drive reports a health warning.

remedies.title: Format a USB stick or drive to work on Windows and Mac
symptoms: use drive on mac and pc
remedies.why: FAT32 can't hold files over 4 GB; NTFS is read-only on Mac; APFS doesn't work on Windows. exFAT works on both.

steps.text: Copy anything you need off the drive first: formatting erases everything on it.
File Explorer › right-click the drive › Format › File system: exFAT › Start.
Disk Utility › select the drive › Erase › Format: ExFAT › Scheme: GUID Partition Map.

remedies.title: Can't eject a drive: "in use"
remedies.why: An app or the system still has a file open on the drive (often Explorer/Finder previews, antivirus or Spotlight).

steps.text: Close files and windows from the drive, then try again.
Wait a minute; indexing or antivirus may be reading it.
Sign out or restart; then remove it.
Removing a drive while it's writing can damage files; wait for activity lights to stop.

remedies.title: Find what's using my space
remedies.why: A few big files and folders usually take most of the disk.

steps.text: Open the Disk map: a picture of your disk, biggest folders first, with the largest files listed.
Settings › System › Storage › Show more categories.
System Settings › General › Storage › the ⓘ next to each category.
